lines.text: With regard to cystic fibrosis, which statement is true?
The answer: it is the most common inherited disease in Caucasians.
(laugh) The sticky mucus child proudly holds the trophy of cystic fibrosis.
The trophy says it all. Cystic fibrosis is the most common inherited disease in Caucasians.
It affects one in two thousand five hundred children.
The worker repairs chromosome seven, where the CFTR gene is mutated. It is autosomal recessive.
Carriers are believed to be relatively more resistant to cholera.
Remember: cystic fibrosis is the most common inherited disease in Caucasians.
With regard to the cerebral circulation, which statement is true?
The answer: cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to changes in the pCO2 of the perfusing blood.
The brain sits above a busy roundabout. This is the circle of Willis, around the base of the brain.
All the main arteries to the brain connect to this rich anastomosis.
So if one artery blocks, the brain is still supplied by the others. There are no functional end-arteries.
(laugh) And the carbon dioxide character turns the tap. Cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to changes in pCO2.
Cerebral blood flow is little affected by cardiovascular reflexes.
Remember: cerebral blood flow is very sensitive to the pCO2 of the blood.
With regard to influenza, which statement is true?
The answer: mutations in the haemagglutinin molecule are responsible for antigenic drift.
The influenza virus drifts down the river in a boat. This is antigenic drift.
(laugh) He uses a wrench to change his spike. That is a mutation in the haemagglutinin molecule.
The host antibodies no longer recognise the new shape, and the virus escapes them.
Epidemics occur through mutations, resulting in amino acid substitutions of the HA and NA.
Pandemics may occur when both are replaced by recombination with animal viruses. That is antigenic shift, and the notable ones were in 1918, 1957 and 1968.
Remember: haemagglutinin mutations cause antigenic drift.
